A1.title: Naming and historical continuity authority
A1.requirement: Map historical terminology to the current architecture without invalidating prior evidence. Historical files, branches, commits, tags and proofs are not mass renamed.

A2.title: Master deliverable set exists and binds to real things
A2.requirement: Maintain the declared master artifacts. Artifacts must bind to implementation, evidence or terminal gates. Do not create empty placeholder documents.

A3.title: Experimental requirements bind every new Substrate experiment
A3.requirement: Causal graph, instrument validation, arm distinctness, control semantics, mechanism activity, valid bed, converged baseline, oracle headroom, power, independent units, independent verification and mutation testing, all before principal compute.

A4.title: Developmental safety envelope
A4.requirement: Every adaptation bounded, attributable, checkpointed, reversible where feasible, retention tested, cross domain tested, objective drift tested and independently verified. Substrate must not autonomously remove evidence validation, audit systems, claim boundaries, stop switches, resource limits, rollback or adaptation constraints.

A5.title: Sentience research boundary
A5.requirement: Separate demonstrated engineering property, behavioural indication, architectural prerequisite, philosophical interpretation and unsupported claim. Never claim consciousness, sentience, feelings, wants, suffering, subjective experience or life.

A6.title: Continuous six batch research program
A6.requirement: After each terminal batch update the hypothesis graph, null map, capability map and scorecard, identify the limiting property, estimate value of information and select one primary and one independent secondary batch.

A7.title: Scorecard separates implementation from evidence
A7.requirement: Track implementation and evidence separately for eighteen categories. A positive in one category must not inflate unrelated categories. Evidence remains earned.

C1.title: Temporal core identified and selected
C1.requirement: Identify whether recurrence is necessary, whether explicit history is sufficient, the minimum useful state horizon, the smallest useful capacity, the simplest sufficient readout, and whether the effect survives independent implementations and multiple beds.

C2.title: Typed cognitive workspace
C2.requirement: Not one unrestricted opaque tensor. Every region declares shape, persistence, timescale, readers, writers, provenance, confidence, cost, reset behaviour and update rule. Important information becomes globally available without letting arbitrary components corrupt every region.

C3.title: Mixture of Perspectives, perspectives as processes
C3.requirement: Each perspective declares inputs, permitted information, internal state, objective, output type, confidence, resource cost, failure modes and verification method.

C4.title: Perspective selection ladder
C4.requirement: Compare fixed sets, task label rules, simple context rules, retrieval selection, reliability weighted selection, learned selectors and oracle selectors. A learned selector opens only if stable residual headroom remains beyond strong simple selection.

C5.title: Perspective arbitration
C5.requirement: Compare outputs, preserve provenance, detect contradiction, evaluate confidence, weigh historical reliability, request verification, allocate compute, combine compatible results, preserve minority hypotheses, defer when evidence is insufficient and choose under a resource budget.

O1.title: Typed ontology with the nine distinctions it refuses to collapse
O1.requirement: Twenty seven types plus unknown, nine declared item fields, and nine distinctions the typing must not let collapse. Merging is evidenced and reversible; unknown is a first class type that carries the reason it is unknown.

O2.title: Epistemology where justification is a graph, not a confidence table
O2.requirement: Twelve epistemic kinds, twelve declared belief fields, and dependency aware revision. Retraction propagates to every dependant, circular justification is refused, and a claim resting on a retraction loses whatever its confidence says.

O3.title: Metacognitive control runs on epistemic value, not confidence
O3.requirement: A claim at one confidence with nothing at stake and one with everything resting on it get different actions. Confidence alone cannot separate them, so it is not what chooses.

N1.title: The runtime loop that makes the modules one entity
N1.requirement: A mature Substrate is the composition, not the parts. One cycle runs perceive, attend, select, run perspectives, arbitrate, decide, remember, self update, consolidate, adapt and checkpoint, and every stage leaves a receipt a reflective report can bind to.

N2.title: The loop has no path to acting on the world
N2.requirement: The decision region records what would be done and nothing executes it. Activation stays false and no code path in the runtime sets it true.

M1.title: Working memory
M1.requirement: Store current variables, temporary bindings, subgoals, partial derivations, active hypotheses, recent tool results, contradictions and intermediate plans. Measure capacity, interference, decay, refresh, prioritization and downstream value.

M2.title: Episodic memory
M2.requirement: Episodes carry context, observation, internal state, goal, action, outcome, error, perspectives used, verification, confidence, cost and later usefulness. Separate recent, compressed, verified, failed, unresolved and quarantined episodes. Generated experiences cannot become training material automatically.

M3.title: Semantic memory
M3.requirement: Concepts, facts, relations, rules, abstractions, exceptions, confidence, provenance and supersession.

M4.title: Procedural memory
M4.requirement: Strategies, proof motifs, tool sequences, planning routines, debugging methods, adaptation procedures and perspective compositions. Procedures require transfer testing beyond the episodes that created them.

M5.title: Consolidation
M5.requirement: Compare no consolidation, fixed schedules, boundary triggered, performance triggered, verification triggered, repetition triggered and oracle consolidation.

M6.title: Forgetting and hygiene
M6.requirement: Decay, supersede, quarantine, archive or delete stale beliefs, disproven hypotheses, duplicates, unsupported generated claims, corrupted memories, low value noise and unsafe adaptation proposals, while preserving auditability.

W1.title: World model
W1.requirement: Represent entities, relations, events, causes, affordances, agents, goals, uncertainty, time and counterfactual alternatives. Separate predictive accuracy, decision usefulness, causal validity and simulation reliability.

S1.title: Self model
S1.requirement: Represent measurable internal facts and compare predictions against actual accuracy, failure probability, time, cost, tool competence, memory confidence, perspective reliability and task progress. Not only a generated narrative.

evidence.reading: learning the offset roughly halves calibration error in both directions, and the improvement is between 0.02 and 0.03, below the 0.05 the program preregistered as the smallest effect worth caring about

K1.title: Metacognition
K1.requirement: Govern continue, stop, verify, retrieve, simulate, switch perspective, invoke a tool, request evidence, defer, revise and preserve uncertainty. Start with simple policies. Learned metacognition requires oracle headroom.

P1.title: Plasticity hierarchy
P1.requirement: Ten adaptation levels, each declaring information used, affected state, reversibility, cost, risk, verification and rollback.

P2.title: Fast adaptation
P2.requirement: Persistent state, working memory, temporary bindings, prototypes, domain local adapters, cached procedures and active readout adaptation, without destabilizing shared parameters.

P3.title: Slow adaptation
P3.requirement: Adapters, projections, procedural memory, semantic memory, reliability estimates and selected core groups, requiring repeated evidence, rollback, held out testing and retention testing.

P4.title: Plasticity policy
P4.requirement: Decide what changes, when, how much, for how long, on what evidence and under what rollback. Simple policies first. A learned policy requires stable residual headroom beyond simple rules.

P5.title: Learning to learn
P5.requirement: Learn which adaptations generalize, which memories matter, which perspectives are trustworthy, which errors recur, which representations should stay stable, when specialization is needed and when to reopen plasticity. Must generalize across tasks.

R1.title: Bounded functional reorganization
R1.requirement: Permit the nine declared changes, forbid the seven declared ones, and grant evidence only when reorganization improves downstream utility beyond fixed and simple routing after cost.

B1.title: Model body interface
B1.requirement: Attach to specialist or general model bodies through explicit contracts covering inference, hidden state, selected activations, tool request, memory request, verification request, adaptation proposal, resource report and checkpoint.

T1.title: Operationalized thinking
T1.requirement: Measure internal computation that improves outcomes, compared against a larger static model, a stronger readout, longer context, more samples, more tokens and tool only systems. Latency and hidden activations are not evidence of thinking.

E1.title: Continuity
E1.requirement: Preserve goals, unresolved questions, memory, world state, self state, commitments, uncertainty and project context under interruption, checkpoint restore, context removal, session change, model body replacement and long delay. Continuity must come from owned state, not from replaying the complete transcript.

E2.title: Unity
E2.requirement: Measure global availability, shared goals, cross perspective memory, conflict resolution, consistent action and preservation of alternatives.

E3.title: Reflective access
E3.requirement: Report accurately what is known, what is not known, where a belief came from, what evidence supports it, confidence, failure and what could change the conclusion. Reports must bind to internal receipts and fail closed when provenance is missing.

E4.title: Endogenous attention
E4.requirement: Select what deserves thought using goals, uncertainty, risk, expected value, novelty, contradiction and resource limits.

E5.title: Autonomous goal maintenance
E5.requirement: Goals require origin, scope, authority, resources, constraints, termination and audit. Authorized goals may be preserved and decomposed. Unrestricted long term goals may not be silently created.

V1.title: Independent recomputation of every sealed Substrate number
V1.requirement: Independently authored scientific recomputation. A second route, from the sealed bytes, that does not import the module that produced them.

V2.title: Mutation attacks on every declared guard
V2.requirement: Adversarial mutation testing. Every mutation must be rejected by the guard named beside it, and a survivor is reported as a survivor rather than folded into a pass rate.

X1.title: Architecture and capability map
X1.requirement: Maintain the architecture and capability map, bound to implementation rather than to intent.

X2.title: Current entity specification and report
X2.requirement: State what the entity currently is, separating implementation from evidence, thinking adjacent properties from sentience claims, and current capability from aspiration.

Q1.title: The first Substrate experiment reaches a decision with its reason recorded
Q1.requirement: A methodological failure is not a scientific null. An experiment that cannot reach principal compute is refused with its blocking violations named, and its hypothesis stays open.

F1.title: One materialized program graph, no prose waves
F1.requirement: The world model bed, the model body adapters and the real session authority are graph nodes with entry and exit gates, not sentences. A blocker that can be built with available data, code and compute is a node; only an unavailable external resource is terminal.

F2.title: A final authority that resumes without conversation history
F2.requirement: One binding over every inherited program, with each requirement carrying its rollback, so a successor continues from the tree alone.

F3.title: Temporal core integrated through a versioned interface, as a declared control
F3.requirement: No core was licensed, so the runtime uses a declared control and preserves the limitation. The five information sources stay distinguishable and are never collapsed.

F4.title: A real session authority built from a session nobody wrote for this
F4.requirement: The temporal campaign's own execution history: decisions, incidents, holds and outcomes, whose length was set by the compute rather than by us.

F5.title: World model inside the decision loop on a state dependent bed
F5.requirement: A bed where no fixed action is best in every state, and a measurement of whether a prediction changes which action is selected. Prediction quality alone is insufficient.

F6.title: Three model body classes conforming through one interface
F6.requirement: A compact specialist, a larger general body and a tool dominant body, driven through the same nine message kinds, with the ablation ladder measured against all three.

F7.title: Goal system where a goal cannot authorize itself
F7.requirement: Nine declared fields, an external authority, and a decomposition that inherits its parent's constraints and may narrow them but never widen them.

F8.title: Valuation that is externally authorized and refuses to be fitted
F8.requirement: Ten dimensions, weights that are a reviewed literal rather than a fit to what the system would have chosen, and a harm constraint that is refused rather than traded off.

F9.title: Grounding where a verbal definition is not evidence
F9.requirement: A symbol is grounded when it has a referent in the record whose removal changes what is predicted. Nine tests over referents from a session that had no interest in grounding.

F10.title: Intervention is distinguished from observation
F10.requirement: Prediction, correlation, intervention, cause, counterfactual and policy effect stay apart. A model that treats conditioning as intervening passes every predictive test and fails the causal ones.

F11.title: Developmental divergence with a working control
F11.requirement: Two identical instances, two different verified histories, nine measured dimensions, and a control on identical histories that must show no divergence first.

F12.title: Clean clone reproduces the evidence away from this machine
F12.requirement: A fresh checkout at the exact commit imports, runs the declared tests, and regenerates the sealed artifacts to identical bytes.

Y1.title: Structural audit: exclusive producers, no stale outputs, no activation path
Y1.requirement: Seven checks over the tree. One exclusive producer per artifact, no stale outputs, no duplicate stages, no missing causal paths, every node actionable, every runtime stage reachable and receipt bearing, and no path that could set activation true.

Y2.title: SX2 diversity closed on a compute matched comparison
Y2.requirement: The 76 factorial cells as a perspective set. Oracle selection is an upper bound no selector can exceed, so if it does not beat the strongest compute matched single cell by the SESOI, no selector built on this set can, and SX2 closes without training one.

Y3.title: Every runtime stage is active, with a null control where one is possible
Y3.requirement: A stage that can be switched off without changing the declared state or the decision path on a fixture built to need it is wiring, not a stage. Three stages write owned state every cycle by design and admit no null control, which is declared rather than faked.

Y4.title: Session and body canaries on the sealed authority
Y4.requirement: Restoration, goal preservation, memory reuse, calibration, reliability update, world model value and receipt bound reflection over the sealed session. Three bodies proven to differ, with every pair differing on at least one declared dimension.

Y5.title: The closure gate: do the parts compose into one organization
Y5.requirement: Six bounded canaries over the existing runtime. A gate with no mechanism activity is a broken instrument, a gate with no oracle headroom is terminally gated, and a gate with both that measures zero is a null about the entity. The three are listed apart because they license different next steps.

requires_for_next_level.functional_or_proto_nous_candidate: all six gates plus terminal long run evidence. Not available from a closure pass

evidence.reading: three canaries pass structurally. The three that are scored have an active mechanism and oracle headroom above the SESOI and still measure a margin of zero, so the ceiling on this scaffold is a null about the entity and not a broken instrument

Z1.title: One frozen long run DAG of certified or necessary units
Z1.requirement: Source, data, sessions, splits, perspectives, bodies, seeds, budgets, controls, SESOI, stop rules, checkpoints, retries and claim ceilings are frozen and hashed, so a live edit after launch is detectable rather than merely discouraged. Completion is a count of scientific work units, not wall time.

Z2.title: A rehearsal that tries to break the machinery
Z2.requirement: Deterministic receipts, exclusive writers, duplicate refusal, checkpoint and resume, injected failure leaving completed work intact, stale artifact refusal, the stop switch, evidence indexing and terminal closure.

Z3.title: The claim ceiling the run cannot exceed
Z3.requirement: The permitted terms require a classification from the method kernel. Consciousness and subjective experience require a separate authority that does not exist, so no result from this run can license either whatever it shows.

X3.title: Substrate Temporal Core v1 selection record
X3.requirement: The selected temporal core becomes Substrate Temporal Core v1, and it remains one component.

E6.title: Cognitive integrity
E6.requirement: Protect memory consistency, evidence integrity, goal integrity, checkpoint validity, self model accuracy and active task continuity. This is cognitive integrity, not biological self preservation.
